issues: The requirement introduces 'shell input' as the object being evaluated, but the evidence only states that eval() was used in scrapy/shell.py without specifying what content is evaluated or its source.

revision_instructions: Remove the reference to 'shell input': the evidence does not specify what content the eval() call evaluates.
Keep the core security guarantee that the evidence does support - that arbitrary code from externally supplied content must not be executed - without naming an unsupported object being evaluated.

results.accepted_requirement: The system shall process XML-RPC request data without exposing the application to the security vulnerabilities associated with unsafe XML parsing.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall process XML-RPC request data without exposing the application to XML-based security vulnerabilities such as entity expansion or external entity attacks.

retrieved_requirements.statement: The system shall not execute arbitrary code originating from externally supplied content.
The system shall prevent user-supplied input from causing arbitrary code to be executed through dynamic module imports.
The system shall prevent untrusted input from causing arbitrary code modules to be loaded and executed during spider generation.

issues: The evidence states only that xmlrpc 'is not inherently safe from vulnerabilities' and that a defused alternative should be used; it does not name the specific attack types (entity expansion, external entity attacks) that the candidate asserts.
The named attack vectors appear to come from general knowledge of XML security rather than from the text of the PR.
revision_instructions: Remove the specific attack types 'entity expansion' and 'external entity attacks': the evidence gives no such detail, only a generic statement that xmlrpc is not inherently safe.

State the requirement at the level of generality the evidence supports: that processing of XML-RPC data must not expose the system to the vulnerabilities associated with unsafe XML parsing, without naming particular attack mechanisms.

retrieved_requirements.statement: The system shall not execute arbitrary code originating from externally supplied content.
The system shall prevent user-supplied input from causing arbitrary code to be executed through dynamic module imports.

issues: The evidence only states that the default value of a named setting was changed to a named class (DownloaderAwarePriorityQueue); it does not describe what observable difference this makes to how requests are scheduled.

As with a named component whose behaviour is inferred from its name rather than stated by the evidence, no rewrite can ground this without inventing the functional effect of 'downloader-aware'.
